Restyle a space, live#

You are walking through a home and want to see it Scandinavian, or Japandi, or with marble floors. Tap a style and the floors, walls, counters, fabrics and skirting change in place on every device, with nothing re-uploaded. People, plants, glass, screens and lamps stay as they are.

Where it is#

  • In the toolbar: Restyle. The panel shows Original and six styles: Scandinavian, Japandi, Luxury Marble, Indian Contemporary, Industrial and Coastal. Each one has a small swatch of its floor.
  • Every preset upholsters the sofa in a real fabric colour, matte (roughness 1, no sheen): oatmeal for Scandinavian, sand for Japandi, champagne for Luxury Marble, terracotta for Indian Contemporary, tobacco for Industrial and sea blue for Coastal. The tints are solved in linear light against the weave's own mean colour. The grey linen weave times a near-white tint used to give a grey sofa in most styles.
  • The text box takes plain words: Scandinavian, luxury marble, Indian contemporary, marble floor, dark wood cabinets, sage green walls, warmer lights, evening. They are understood on the device, so no AI service is involved and the same words always give the same result.
  • Hold: before shows the original while you hold it down. Undo steps back one change. Copy link copies a link that opens with the style you have on screen.
  • Clip 9:16 / 16:9 records a 15-second before-and-after clip (on desktop only).

What changes, and what never does#

Every material in the file gets a role from its name and from where its surfaces sit (how much faces up or sideways, how high it sits, how big it is). The compiler writes these facts into the scene, so the viewer reads them when the scene opens and does not have to scan anything.

RestyledNever touched
floors (wood, stone, tile), walls (paint, plaster, stone), ceilings, skirting, counters, cabinets and joinery, upholstery, leather, rugs, curtains, metal trimglass and mirrors, people, plants, screens, lamps and emissive surfaces, decor (books, art, vases), anything the classifier is not sure about

A style swaps in a texture from the built-in material library (26 CC0 sets from ambientCG; see attributions). The texture is laid out in world metres from three directions (triplanar mapping), so a plank is a plank wide on every floor whatever the file's UVs look like. It does not stretch on badly unwrapped meshes, and there are no seams where one mesh meets another. Paint styles are a flat colour with the room's lighting kept. On a baked scene the new surface keeps the bake's light and shadow, because the bake's brightness is carried over.

Each style also sets a lighting mood through the light studio: exposure, environment fill and a white balance (warmer or cooler). The sun stays where the scene or the Sun panel put it. The white balance applies to the room's surfaces only. Glass, people and plants keep their colour.

Speed#

The first time a style is used, its textures are fetched (about 60 KB each, 512² JPEG) and uploaded. After that a switch between styles takes less than 300 ms, crossfade included (on WebGPU and on WebGL2; measured by web/test/fix-verify-restyle.mjs). Streamed scenes use 8 of the 12 layers in the media texture array (the other 4 hold video screens). Classic and Fidelity scenes have 16 slots of their own. When a slot is needed, the style used longest ago gives up its slot.

Links#

?style= carries the look, for example:

Code
/app?vpk=…&style=japandi
/app?vpk=…&style=japandi;floor-stone=marble-white;floor-stone.r=0.15;w=0.60

A preset id comes first, then any per-role changes (role=set, role.t=rrggbb tint, role.r= roughness, role.m=0|1 metal) and the mood (ev=, env=, w= warmth −1…1). The address bar follows every change, so the link people copy always carries the current look.

Tour together#

In a live tour room, a host who restyles changes the look for everyone. The change goes to the room as the presenter action { name: "style", detail: { style: "<the ?style= value>", query: "<same>" } } (style is the field the presenter reads; query is kept for older clients). Followers apply it through window.__verseSetStyle(style), which goes through the same path as the panel. An empty style restores the original.

For generators and modellers: the naming contract#

When the material names follow the pattern below, the role comes from the name before any guessing. The Verse Home generator (plan-to-home) uses this pattern. Names are split on _, -, ., spaces and camelCase, numbers are dropped, and matching ignores case. The first word decides the role. A later word can choose a material family:

Material nameRole
floor_<room>floor-wood
floor_<room>_tile (also ceramic, porcelain, mosaic)floor-tile
floor_<room>_stone (also marble, granite, concrete, terrazzo, travertine)floor-stone
wall_<room>wall-paint
wall_<room>_plaster (also render, stucco, limewash)wall-plaster
wall_<room>_tile (also stone, marble, brick, concrete)wall-stone
ceiling_<room>ceiling
skirting[_<room>], baseboardskirting
counter[_<room>], countertop, worktop, benchtopcountertop
cabinet_…, wardrobe_…, door_…, joinery_…, shelf_…, table_…, desk_…cabinet-wood
sofa_…, chair_…, armchair_…, bed_…, cushion_…, fabric_… (add _leather for leather)upholstery-fabric / leather
rug_…, carpet_…rug
curtain_…, drape_…, blind_…curtain
metal_…, trim_…, handle_…, tap_…, fitting_…metal-trim
person_…, people_…, figure_…people (protected)
plant_…, tree_…, foliage_…plant (protected)
glass_…, glazing_…, window_…, mirror_…glass (protected)
screen_…, tv_…, monitor_…screen (protected)
light_…, lamp_…, emitter_…, bulb_…light (protected)
decor_…, art_…, vase_…, book_…decor (protected)

Examples: floor_kitchen_tile, wall_living, wall_bath_tile, ceiling_bedroom_2, skirting, counter_kitchen. Give each room its own floor, wall and ceiling materials so a later "marble in the kitchen only" can address one room. A material with transmission (or blended with alpha under 0.6) is always glass, whatever its name.

Verse Home's generator uses the contract as is, with no new roles: sofas, beds, cushions and dining-chair seats are sofa_fabric / cushion_fabric_accent / bed_linen; drapes are curtain_drape; kitchen shutters cabinet_kitchen_shutter; table tops table_top; the TV feature wall is joinery_feature_<room> (wood slats) or wall_<room>_feature_marble / _concrete (stone); rug borders rug_border; lamp shades, the cove LED and downlights lamp_shade, light_cove, light_downlight (protected); the furniture pack's models keep decor_… names except a chair's legs (cabinet_wood_…), so a restyle changes the soft goods, joinery and surfaces and leaves the hero pieces, art and plants as photographed. The window view is decor_view_city, and any decor_view_… material is scenery to the compiler too (no collision, outside the walk grid).

Files that do not follow the pattern are still classified, from words in the name (Wood_Floor, Parquet, White Paint, linen) and then from geometry: a large up-facing surface at floor level is a floor, a tall sideways one is a wall, and a large down-facing one at the top is a ceiling. Anything uncertain is left alone.

Programmatic#

  • window.verseApp.restyle({ preset: "japandi" }) and window.__verseRestyle.apply(action) (dev and staging; production keeps the app's plumbing off window — handover/production-hardening.md, tier
    1. take a restyle action: { preset?, changes?: [{ role, set?, flat?, tint?, tintMul?, roughness?, metal? }], lights?: { ev?, env?, warmth?, sun?: [azimuth, elevation, intensity] }, reset?, undo? } (a sun here moves the sun until the style is cleared). Unknown roles, library sets and out-of-range values are dropped.
  • window.__verseRestyle.say("marble floor, warmer lights") runs the same free-text grammar as the panel.
  • window.__verseRestyle.roles() lists every material with its role, a confidence and the reasons, so you can see why Floor_02 became floor-wood.
  • A verse-restyle window event fires on every change (detail: { name: "style", query, state, ms }).

Gate#

web/test/fix-verify-restyle.mjs checks the grammar, the naming contract and the classifier. On the unbaked two-room interior (with a person, a plant and a glass partition added) and on the villa when it is present, it checks on tier A and on tier C (phone class): every panel style visibly changes the floor and the walls; glass, people and plants match the same lighting mood applied on its own; tier C matches tier A; switches take ≤ 300 ms; memory stays ≤ 256 MB on a phone; there are no console errors; Original restores the first frame; the room action and the ?style= link reproduce the host's frame. Frames are saved to web/test/out/restyle/.
